base_method_text.title:
Let 2D Diffusion Model Know 3D-Consistency for Robust Text-to-3D
  Generation
base_method_text.summary:
Text-to-3D generation has shown rapid progress in recent days with the advent
of score distillation, a methodology of using pretrained text-to-2D diffusion
models to optimize neural radiance field (NeRF) in the zero-shot setting.
However, the lack of 3D awareness in the 2D diffusion models destabilizes score
distillation-based methods from reconstructing a plausible 3D scene. To address
this issue, we propose 3DFuse, a novel framework that incorporates 3D awareness
into pretrained 2D diffusion models, enhancing the robustness and 3D
consistency of score distillation-based methods. We realize this by first
constructing a coarse 3D structure of a given text prompt and then utilizing
projected, view-specific depth map as a condition for the diffusion model.
Additionally, we introduce a training strategy that enables the 2D diffusion
model learns to handle the errors and sparsity within the coarse 3D structure
for robust generation, as well as a method for ensuring semantic consistency
throughout all viewpoints of the scene. Our framework surpasses the limitations
of prior arts, and has significant implications for 3D consistent generation of
2D diffusion models.
base_method_text.main_contributions: The paper addresses the 3D inconsistency problem in text-to-3D generation by introducing 3DFuse, a framework that incorporates 3D awareness into pretrained 2D diffusion models. Key contributions include a consistency injection module using point cloud depth maps and semantic coding to enhance 3D consistency and reduce semantic ambiguity.
base_method_text.methodology: 3DFuse uses a consistency injection module that conditions a 2D diffusion model on projected depth maps of coarse 3D structures generated from text prompts. It employs semantic code sampling to reduce text prompt ambiguity and Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) to ensure semantic consistency. The framework leverages an off-the-shelf point cloud generation model and finetunes a conditioning module within the diffusion model.
base_method_text.experimental_setup: The method was evaluated on text-to-3D generation using DreamFusion, SJC, and ProlificDreamer baselines with Stable Diffusion. Qualitative analysis, ablation studies, and a novel metric using COLMAP were used to assess 3D consistency. A user study with 102 participants was also conducted to evaluate 3D coherence, prompt adherence, and rendering quality.
base_method_text.limitations: The approach relies on the pretrained diffusion model's ability to follow text prompts and may inherit societal biases present in the training dataset. The method also has difficulty in reflecting complex user prompts faithfully.
base_method_text.future_research_directions: Future research directions include addressing the difficulty in reflecting complex user prompts faithfully and mitigating societal biases inherited from the dataset, similar to text-to-image generation models.

add_method_texts.title:
NExT-Mol: 3D Diffusion Meets 1D Language Modeling for 3D Molecule
  Generation
add_method_texts.summary:
3D molecule generation is crucial for drug discovery and material design.
While prior efforts focus on 3D diffusion models for their benefits in modeling
continuous 3D conformers, they overlook the advantages of 1D SELFIES-based
Language Models (LMs), which can generate 100% valid molecules and leverage the
billion-scale 1D molecule datasets. To combine these advantages for 3D molecule
generation, we propose a foundation model -- NExT-Mol: 3D Diffusion Meets 1D
Language Modeling for 3D Molecule Generation. NExT-Mol uses an extensively
pretrained molecule LM for 1D molecule generation, and subsequently predicts
the generated molecule's 3D conformers with a 3D diffusion model. We enhance
NExT-Mol's performance by scaling up the LM's model size, refining the
diffusion neural architecture, and applying 1D to 3D transfer learning.
Notably, our 1D molecule LM significantly outperforms baselines in
distributional similarity while ensuring validity, and our 3D diffusion model
achieves leading performances in conformer prediction. Given these improvements
in 1D and 3D modeling, NExT-Mol achieves a 26% relative improvement in 3D FCD
for de novo 3D generation on GEOM-DRUGS, and a 13% average relative gain for
conditional 3D generation on QM9-2014. Our codes and pretrained checkpoints are
available at https://github.com/acharkq/NExT-Mol.
add_method_texts.main_contributions: The paper introduces NExT-Mol, a foundation model for 3D molecule generation that combines the strengths of 1D SELFIES-based Language Models (LMs) and 3D diffusion models. Key contributions include a novel diffusion model (DMT) for 3D conformer prediction and a transfer learning approach to leverage 1D molecule sequence data for improved 3D conformer prediction, achieving state-of-the-art performance in de novo and conditional 3D molecule generation.
add_method_texts.methodology: NExT-Mol employs a two-step approach: first, a Molecular Llama LM (MoLlama) generates a 1D molecule sequence using autoregressive transformers. Second, a Diffusion Molecular Transformer (DMT) predicts the 3D conformer from the 1D sequence, using Relational Multi-Head Self-Attention (RMHA) and adaptive layer normalization. Transfer learning is used to incorporate MoLlama's 1D representations into DMT.
add_method_texts.experimental_setup: The model was evaluated on GEOM-DRUGS, GEOM-QM9, and QM9-2014 datasets. De novo and conditional 3D molecule generation were assessed using metrics like FCD, atom stability, molecular stability, and geometric similarity. 3D conformer prediction was evaluated using Coverage (COV) and Average Minimum RMSD (AMR). Baselines include CDGS, JODO, MiDi, G-SchNet, G-SphereNet, EDM, MDM, GeoLDM, EEGSDE, EQGAT-diff, MolGPT, MolGen, OMEGA, GeoMol, GeoDiff, Torsional Diffusion, Particle Guidance, and MCF.
add_method_texts.limitations: The paper acknowledges limitations including the generalization of 3D conformer prediction to unseen scaffolds, not exploring randomized SELFIES data augmentation in pretraining, and not exploring pretrained molecular large LM with bi-directional Self-Attention. It also mentions the computational cost when incorporating MoLlama for 3D Conformer Prediction and the quadratic memory complexity of DMT’s Pair Representation.
add_method_texts.future_research_directions: Future research directions include extending NExT-Mol to process multiple molecular inputs for structure-based molecule design, modeling interactions between small molecules and proteins/RNAs, exploring diffusion guidance methods, and applying model editing techniques to update the model's knowledge according to application requirements. The authors also plan to build multi-modal foundation models with NExT-Mol as the backbone for tasks like chemical reaction prediction and drug-drug interaction prediction.

new_method:
Below is an example of a possible new method (step 3) that draws on both the Base Method (3DFuse’s 3D‐aware diffusion pipeline) and the Add Method (NExT‐Mol’s two‐stage approach using a large‐scale 1D language model plus a 3D diffusion model). This method is intended to address challenges such as unstable geometry and limited robustness to complex text prompts, going beyond minor adjustments to the Base Method:

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
STEP 3: PROPOSED NEW METHOD
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
We introduce “Latent‐Bridge Diffusion,” a framework that first parses a user’s text prompt with a specialized large language model (LLM) to derive a structured representation of the scene (the “Latent Bridge”) before performing 3D consistency‐aware synthesis via a diffusion backbone. Specifically:

1) Hierarchical Text Parsing.  
   • Use a pretrained LLM (similar to the 1D SELFIES‐based LM in NExT‐Mol, but adapted for natural‐language scene descriptors) to parse the prompt into a set of object descriptors, spatial relations, and attributes.  
   • This converts an unstructured text prompt into a more fine‐grained “1D scene grammar,” where each object has a conceptual label and high‐level geometry hints (shape descriptors, size, position constraints).

2) Latent‐Bridge Representation.  
   • The “1D scene grammar” is then encoded into a latent representation (e.g., via an autoregressive transformer).  
   • This encoded scene grammar—similar in principle to NExT‐Mol’s representation of molecular graphs—ensures that the final diffusion steps have consistent knowledge about each object’s role and approximate spatial arrangement.

3) 3D Diffusion with Structured Conditioning.  
   • A 3D‐aware diffusion model (inspired by 3DFuse) is conditioned not only on random coarse geometry (as in the Base Method) but also on the Latent Bridge.  
   • This conditioning step injects object‐level constraints, so that the diffusion process “knows” which objects appear where and how they ought to relate or intersect.

4) Iterative Correction Module.  
   • During generation, the diffusion model periodically refines the coarse 3D shape.  
   • At each refinement step, it reconsiders the Latent Bridge cues (e.g., verifying that the partially generated geometry aligns with object descriptors).  
   • View‐specific depth maps are projected as in 3DFuse, but now guided by the object‐level constraints from the LLM’s representation, helping stabilize complex prompts involving multiple objects or intricate spatial layouts.

5) Multi‐Modal Consistency Check.  
   • After each refinement, a cross‐modal “consistency check” ensures that the scene still corresponds to the textual description embedded in the Latent Bridge.  
   • Any ambiguities are flagged and corrected by re‐evaluating the relevant segment of the LLM‐generated grammar.

By introducing a dedicated LLM‐based parsing stage (inspired by NExT‐Mol’s 1D modeling) and injecting that structured scene representation into a 3D diffusion loop (inspired by the Base Method), Latent‐Bridge Diffusion addresses both the difficulty of robustly handling complex multi‐object prompts and the fragility of purely 2D‐conditioned 3D generation. This is a genuinely new pipeline that integrates the high‐level strengths of large language modeling with a view‐dependent 3D diffusion backbone for stable and semantically consistent text‐to‐3D results.
